title: Describing words
examples: Can you tell me what an adjective is?
How do I use describing words?

explain.say: Today you will learn describing words. These words tell you about things.

items: Words tell us more about nouns

explain.say: A describing word tells you what something is like.
Big is a describing word. Big tells you about size.
Soft tells you how something feels when you touch it.
Shiny tells you how something looks in the light.
Look at this red ball. You can say it is big and shiny.

faq.q: What is the difference between a describing word and a naming word?
faq.a: A naming word names a person, place or thing, like dog. A describing word tells you more about it, like big.
asks: Can you give me an example of a describing word?
Does a describing word name something?

faq.q: Can I use describing words at the beginning of a sentence?
faq.a: Yes, you can. For example, soft grass is nice to sit on.
asks: Is it okay to start with 'blue'?
Can adjectives go first in a sentence?

faq.q: Do I need to use a describing word every time?
faq.a: No. Sometimes the naming word is enough. Describing words add more detail.
asks: Is it always best to describe things?

faq.q: What kind of things can describing words describe?
faq.a: They can describe people, animals and things. They tell you about size, colour or how something feels.
asks: Can I describe feelings with these words?
Do they only describe things I can see?

faq.q: Are 'big' and 'large' the same describing word?
faq.a: They mean almost the same thing. Both words tell us that something is of a great size.
asks: Can I swap them in a sentence?

facts: Describing words are also called adjectives.
They tell us more about nouns.
Words like big, soft and shiny are adjectives.
Adjectives can describe size, colour and how things feel.

quiz.say: Look at the kitten. Which word describes its fur?
quiz.why: Fluffy tells you what the fur is like.

wrong.0: Running is a doing word, and it tells what the kitten does.
wrong.2: Kitten is a naming word, and it names the animal.

quiz.say: Which word tells you the size of the apple?
quiz.why: Big tells you how large the apple is.

wrong.0: Red is a describing word for colour, and the question asks about size.
wrong.1: Shiny tells how the apple looks, and the question asks about size.

quiz.say: Think about a teddy bear. Which word tells how it feels to touch?
quiz.why: Soft tells you how the teddy feels when you hold it.

wrong.1: Loud tells about a sound, and a teddy is quiet.
wrong.2: Blue tells about colour, and the question asks how it feels.
